iamTemplates.description: Pick a ready-made policy. You can attach it to a user or token now, or later from the policy list.
iamTemplates.attachIdRequired: Enter the ID to attach to, or choose Nothing yet.

aiControl.title: AI control
aiControl.description: Decide what agents and the built-in assistant may do on this instance. The server enforces this on every request, whatever the token allows.
aiControl.navDescription: Turn agent access off, read-only or on, and limit it to chosen environments.

off.label: Off
off.description: Every agent request is refused. Humans are not affected.

observe.label: Observe
observe.description: Agents can read apps, logs and metrics, but not secrets, and change nothing.

operate.label: Operate
operate.description: Agents can read, write and deploy in the environments below. They cannot use root, change secrets, backups or instance settings.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: Agents can use any ability their token holds in the environments below. A person must still approve protected deploys.

aiControl.adminUnavailable: Admin mode needs the experimental feature ai-control to be enabled on the server.
aiControl.envKindsDescription: Applies to operate and admin. Apps with no environment count as custom.
aiControl.viewAudit: View agent activity in the audit log

revoke.title: Revoke every agent token?
revoke.description: Every token with an agent label stops working immediately. This cannot be undone. The built-in assistant keeps working.

aiControl.loadFailed: Could not load AI control settings.

tokens.emptyBody: Create a scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
tokens.name: Name

create.title: Create token
create.description: A scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
create.name: Name
create.agentTip: Label the token as issued to an AI agent, for example "Claude Code". The name is shown here and on every audit log entry the token makes, so you can tell agent changes from human ones.
create.rootExclusive: Root cannot be combined with other abilities
create.signInApproveHint: Lets this token show your sign-in codes and approve new browsers from the CLI. Root does not include it and a device login never grants it. It must expire within 30 days and is revoked when you change or reset your password or sign out your other sessions.
create.signInApproveExpiry: A token that approves sign-ins must expire within 30 days
create.signInApproveAgent: A token that approves sign-ins cannot be issued to an agent
create.secretsRevealHint: Lets this token read a secret value, but only when the server allows token reveal (APP_SECRET_REVEAL_TOKENS=on) and the request carries your password. Every reveal is audited. Root does not include it.

hostFirewall.title: Host firewall
hostFirewall.description: Turns this server's ufw firewall on or off. Turning it on first allows SSH, the control plane ports and HTTP/3, so you cannot lock yourself out.
hostFirewall.confirmOnBody: These commands will run on this server, in order. SSH is allowed before the firewall is switched on.
hostFirewall.confirmOffBody: All ports on this server will be reachable again. This runs:
hostFirewall.missingHelp: Install ufw on this server to manage its firewall from here, or use your cloud provider's firewall.
hostFirewall.sshNote: SSH is on a different port? Set APP_FIREWALL_SSH_PORTS on the control plane before turning this on.

databaseUpgrades.formDescription: Databases inherit this until you override them on their Upgrades tab. Only the platform owner can change it.

githubApp.manageAccessHint: Missing a repository? Choose which repositories this app can see on GitHub, then come back.

owner.legend: Who owns the App on GitHub
owner.orgHelp: The organization you want to deploy from. You need permission to create GitHub Apps there.
owner.orgInvalid: Use the organization's login: letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 39 characters.
owner.allowOthers: Allow other accounts and organizations to install it
owner.publicHelp: Any GitHub account or organization can install this App. Pick this when you deploy from several organizations.

preview.appNameHelp: The one field GitHub itself lets you change on its own confirmation page too.

githubApp.notInstalled: The App was created but has not been installed on an account or organization yet. Finish installing it on GitHub to pick repositories. A private App can only be installed on the account or organization that owns it.

dockerGuard.title: Docker API guard
dockerGuard.description: Every Docker request this control plane makes passes through an allowlist that blocks privileged containers, host namespaces and protected host mounts.

enforce.label: Enforce
enforce.description: Reject requests a rule denies before they reach Docker.

audit.label: Audit
audit.description: Allow everything and record what enforce would deny.

off.label: Off
off.description: No guard. Takes effect after a restart.

dockerGuard.notConfigured: This control plane was started without the guard.
dockerGuard.restartRequired: The saved mode differs from the running one. Restart the control plane to apply it.
dockerGuard.readyToEnforce: Audit mode saw no would-be denials in the last {{days}} days. Enforce is likely safe.
dockerGuard.pinned: The mode is set by APP_DOCKER_GUARD on the server. Unset it to change the mode here.

githubAppOrg.addOrgHelp: GitHub shows the accounts you can install on. Pick the organization. If you are not an owner, GitHub sends the request to its owners.
githubAppOrg.privateTitle: This GitHub App is private, so GitHub only allows it on the account that owns it.
githubAppOrg.privateBody: To add an organization, open the App's Advanced settings, choose Make public (Any account), then come back and press Add organization. Or register a new App owned by the organization.
githubAppOrg.makePublic: Make the App public on GitHub
githubAppOrg.noSlug: This connection was registered before Levelrail could remember the App's install link. Reconnect the App above (or use manual setup) to enable Add organization here.

oauthPage.callbackCopyFailed: Could not copy. Select the URL and copy it by hand.

issuerUrl.label: Issuer URL
issuerUrl.hint: Your identity provider's OIDC issuer, the address /.well-known/openid-configuration is served from.

securityPage.title: Security
securityPage.description: Sessions, two-factor authentication, passkeys, and login protection for this account.

banner.title: Sign-in relies on a password alone
banner.body: Turn on two-factor authentication or register a passkey so a leaked password cannot open this dashboard on its own.

account.title: Your sign-in methods
account.description: Two-factor authentication, passkeys, your password and active sessions live on your Account page.

loginProtection.title: Login protection
loginProtection.body: Failed sign-in attempts are rate limited per IP address and username, with each additional failure making the next allowed attempt wait longer than the last. A handful of mistyped passwords will never lock you out, but repeated automated guessing gets slower with every try.

controlPlaneHealth.title: Control plane health
controlPlaneHealth.description: Live saturation of this instance: process, database, reconcile loop and open streams.
controlPlaneHealth.allClear: Every measurement is under its threshold.
controlPlaneHealth.noSlowQueries: No slow queries recorded since start.

integrity.title: Database integrity
integrity.notYet: No check has run since this process started. The first one runs shortly.
integrity.noSnapshots: No snapshots exist yet. Create one from the backups page.
integrity.pending: Snapshot {{name}} replaces the database at the next start.
integrity.staged: Restore staged. Restart the control plane to apply it.
integrity.confirmDescription: The snapshot is verified again before it is staged, and applied during the next start before the database opens.
integrity.consequenceKept: The current database file is kept beside it, not deleted.
integrity.consequenceRestart: Changes made after the snapshot was taken are not in it.

guard.title: Reconcile protection
guard.summary: {{deferred}} passes were deferred, {{recent}} limited in the last 5 minutes, {{open}} breakers open.
guard.none: No controller has tripped a breaker or hit a rate limit.

loops.title: Background loops
loops.empty: No background loops have reported yet.
loops.row: every {{every}} s, {{runs}} runs, last {{ms}} ms, cost {{cost}} % of one core

reconcile_breakers.title: A controller keeps failing and was paused
reconcile_breakers.hint: Its breaker retries on a growing delay. Fix the cause shown below, then reset protection to retry now.

reconcile_storm.title: A burst of events hit the rate limit
reconcile_storm.hint: Passes were merged so the host stays responsive. Resetting protection refills the budget.

db_integrity.title: The control plane database is damaged
db_integrity.hint: Restore the newest verified snapshot. It is applied at the next start and the damaged file is kept.

rss.title: High memory use
rss.hint: The process is using a lot of RAM. Lower APP_GOMEMLIMIT_PERCENT or review the loops below.

threads.title: Many OS threads
threads.hint: Usually blocked disk or network calls. Restart the control plane if it keeps climbing.

telemetry_size.title: Metrics database is large
telemetry_size.hint: Pruning applies the retention and size cap, then returns free space to the disk.

goroutines.title: Many goroutines
goroutines.hint: Usually open streams or stuck jobs. Restart the control plane if it keeps climbing.

heap.title: High memory use
heap.hint: Check for very large log or build outputs held in memory.

db_latency.title: Slow database queries
db_latency.hint: Refreshing query statistics often restores good plans.

db_queue.title: Writes are queueing
db_queue.hint: The single SQLite writer is busy. Look at the slow query list below.

wal_size.title: Write ahead log is large
wal_size.hint: A checkpoint folds it back into the database file.

slow_queries.title: Many slow queries
slow_queries.hint: Review the list below, then clear the counter once handled.

reconcile_pass.title: Reconcile pass is slow
reconcile_pass.hint: A controller is taking long. The slowest one is shown in the metrics.

event_lag.title: Reconcile loop is lagging
event_lag.hint: No pass finished recently. Restart the control plane if this persists.

streams.title: Live streams near the cap
streams.hint: New log and event streams are refused at the cap. Raise APP_MAX_LIVE_STREAMS if the host has headroom.

generalPage.title: General
generalPage.description: What this instance is running on, how much disk it has left, and which core features are configured.

density.title: Interface density
density.description: Compact fits more on screen. Comfortable adds spacing. Stored in this browser only.

banner.dockerBody: The control plane cannot talk to the Docker engine, so nothing can be deployed or reconciled until it comes back.
banner.secretsBody: Environment secrets cannot be stored until a master key is set for this instance.

width.title: Page width
width.description: How wide page content gets on large screens. Screens under 1024px are not affected. Stored in this browser only.
width.comfortableHint: Centered column with generous side margins

emailPage.title: Email
emailPage.description: The backend that sends alert notifications and password-reset links.

banner.title: No email backend is configured
banner.body: Alert emails and password-reset links will not be sent until you pick SMTP, Amazon SES, or Resend below.

emailDelivery.title: Email delivery
emailDelivery.secretSet: Already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

sender.title: Sender
sender.description: Who the mail comes from. Every provider uses these.
sender.envelopeHelp: Where bounces go. Leave blank to use the from address.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: How mail is delivered. Pick one and fill in its details.

smtp.presets: Quick fill for a known relay

ses.regionHelp: The AWS region where your sender identity is verified.

sesSmtp.credentialsTitle: SES SMTP credentials are not your IAM keys
sesSmtp.credentialsBody: Create SMTP credentials in the SES console (SMTP settings) and enter that username and password here. IAM access keys will be rejected.

limits.title: Delivery limits
limits.description: Caps that protect your provider account from a runaway loop. Sends over the cap fail fast and show in the log.
limits.zeroHelp: 0 uses the server default, which is unlimited unless set.

security.title: Security
security.description: How the connection to the mail server is protected.
security.verifyOff: Certificate checks are off. Anyone between this server and the mail server could read or change your mail. Only do this for a trusted private network.
security.apiNote: This provider is reached over HTTPS with a verified certificate. There is nothing to configure here.

test.title: Send a test email
test.description: Sends one real message through the saved provider, the same path alerts and password resets use. Leave the address blank to send to yourself.

auth_failed.title: The provider rejected the credentials
auth_failed.fix: Re-enter the password or API key and save again. Check that the username belongs to the same account.
auth_failed.fixSesSmtp: SES SMTP credentials are generated in the SES console and are not the same as IAM access keys. Create SMTP credentials there and paste the username and password here.

sender_not_verified.title: The sender address is not verified
sender_not_verified.fix: Verify the from address or its whole domain in the provider console, then send the test again.

region_mismatch.title: Sender verified in a different region
region_mismatch.fix: Pick the region where the sender identity is verified, or verify it in the selected region.

port_blocked.title: Could not reach the mail server
port_blocked.fix: Check the host and port. Many clouds block port 25, so try 587 or 465, and check any firewall in front of this server.

tls_error.title: The secure connection failed
tls_error.fix: Match the TLS mode to the port (STARTTLS on 587, TLS on 465). For a private server with its own certificate, turn off certificate verification under Security.

rate_limited.title: Sending is rate limited
rate_limited.fix: The provider or the send cap set here is throttling. Wait a minute and retry, or raise the cap under Delivery limits.

not_configured.title: No provider is set up
not_configured.fix: Choose a provider, fill in its details and save before sending a test.

other.title: The send failed
other.fix: Read the provider response below. If it is unclear, check the provider dashboard for the rejected message.

domain.title: Sender domain check
domain.description: Looks up SPF, DKIM and DMARC for your from address domain, so mail lands in the inbox instead of spam.

codes.spf_missing: No SPF record. Publish a TXT record starting with v=spf1 that authorizes your provider.
codes.spf_multiple: More than one SPF record exists. Merge them into one, receivers reject duplicates.
codes.spf_permissive: SPF ends in +all, which authorizes any sender. Use ~all or -all.
codes.spf_no_include: SPF does not include {{include}}. Add include:{{include}} unless your provider uses its own return-path domain.
codes.dkim_not_found: No DKIM key found at common selectors. Add the DKIM records your provider shows on its domain verification page.
codes.dmarc_ok: A DMARC policy that quarantines or rejects is published.
codes.dmarc_monitor_only: DMARC is in monitor mode (p=none). Move to quarantine or reject once SPF and DKIM pass.
codes.dmarc_missing: No DMARC record. Publish a TXT record at _dmarc with v=DMARC1; p=none to start monitoring.

providerHints.ses: SES: verify the domain under Verified identities and publish the three DKIM CNAME records it gives you.
providerHints.ses_smtp: SES: verify the domain under Verified identities and publish the three DKIM CNAME records it gives you.
providerHints.resend: Resend: add the domain under Domains and publish the SPF and DKIM records it lists, then wait for it to show Verified.

auth.dockerhub: Use your Docker Hub username with a personal access token, not your account password.
auth.ghcr: Use your GitHub username with a personal access token (classic).
auth.gitlab: Use a deploy token or a personal access token as the password.
auth.ecr: The username is always AWS. The password is the output of aws ecr get-login-password, valid for 12 hours.
auth.gar: The username is _json_key and the password is the service account key JSON.
auth.acr: Use a repository scoped token or a service principal: the username is the token name or app id, the password is its secret.
auth.harbor: Use a robot account: the username looks like robot$name and the password is its secret.
auth.quay: Use a robot account: the username is org+robotname and the password is its token.
auth.jfrog: The username is your user and the password is an identity token, not your account password.
auth.nexus: Use the username and password of a user with access to the Docker repository.
auth.generic: Any registry that speaks the Docker Registry HTTP API v2 with basic authentication.

scopes.dockerhub: Read-only access is enough to pull. Choose Read & Write only if builds push.
scopes.ghcr: read:packages to pull, write:packages to push. For an SSO-enforced organization, authorize the token for SSO.
scopes.gitlab: read_registry to pull, write_registry to push. A deploy token is scoped to one project or group.
scopes.ecr: ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer and ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, from a key or a role.
scopes.gar: roles/artifactregistry.reader to pull, roles/artifactregistry.writer to push.
scopes.acr: The AcrPull role (or a token with content/read) to pull, AcrPush to push.
scopes.harbor: Pull permission on the project the images live in.
scopes.jfrog: Read permission on the Docker repository.
scopes.generic: Pull access to the repositories you deploy.

empty.title: No storage destinations
empty.description: Connect AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO, Wasabi, any S3-compatible bucket, or an enrolled node to store backups, archives and dumps.

controlPlaneDrKeygen.title: New backup recipient key
controlPlaneDrKeygen.description: The public key is added to the backup recipients. The private key is shown once and is never stored on this server.
controlPlaneDrKeygen.warning: Store the private key offline now (a password manager or a safe). Without it the backups cannot be decrypted.
controlPlaneDrKeygen.use: I saved it, add the public key

controlPlaneDrRestore.title: Restore plan
controlPlaneDrRestore.description: Recovery replaces the control plane database, so it runs on the host with the control plane stopped. These are the steps for this install.
controlPlaneDrRestore.noBackup: No complete off-box backup exists yet. Run a backup before you rely on recovery.

warnings.escrow_not_acknowledged: The master key escrow is not acknowledged: a restore without the master key cannot read stored secrets.
warnings.drill_not_passed: No restore drill has passed yet, so this plan is untested.

backup_available.title: A complete backup is available
backup_available.body: The newest encrypted backup at the destination has both its data and manifest.

identity_ready.title: Have a private key ready
identity_ready.body: You need the private key that matches one of the backup recipients.

master_key_escrow.title: Have the master key escrow ready
master_key_escrow.body: The backup does not contain the master key. Restore it from your escrow bundle.

stop_control_plane.title: Stop the control plane
stop_control_plane.body: Restore refuses to run while the database is in use.

run_restore.title: Run the restore on the host
run_restore.body: The current database is kept next to the restored one as a pre-restore copy.

start_and_verify.title: Start the control plane and verify
start_and_verify.body: Check that apps, domains and nodes are back, then run a fresh backup.

iacPage.title: Infrastructure as code
iacPage.description: Describe projects, environments, apps, domains and databases as YAML, review the plan, then apply it.
iacPage.filesDescription: One or more YAML documents separated by ---. Documents never hold secret values, reference them with secretRef.
iacPage.sourceHint: Tags the apps this apply creates so prune can find them later.
iacPage.prune: Prune: delete apps this source created that the files no longer declare
iacPage.noDeploy: Do not restart running apps to apply env changes
iacPage.confirmSummary: {{create}} to create, {{update}} to update, {{delete}} to delete.
iacPage.confirmNote: The apply only proceeds if live state still matches the plan you reviewed.

githubManualDialog.title: Connect a GitHub App manually
githubManualDialog.descSuffix: (or your GitHub Enterprise Server instance's own /settings/apps/new), then paste the resulting credentials here. No primary domain required to save these: only automated setup needs one.
githubManualDialog.instanceHint: Leave blank for github.com. Self-hosted instances work too, e.g. https://github.example.com.
githubManualDialog.webhookHint: The value you set as the App's own webhook secret on GitHub, not generated here.
githubManualDialog.privateKeyHint: Generated once on the App's General page on GitHub and downloaded as a .pem file. Paste its full contents.
githubManualDialog.connectFailed: Could not connect the GitHub App.

drCard.title: Disaster recovery
drCard.description: Encrypted off-box backups, key escrow and restore drills.
drCard.identityConfigured: configured, drills decrypt and restore fully
drCard.identityMissing: not configured, drills verify checksums only (APP_CONTROL_PLANE_DRILL_IDENTITY_FILE)

buildCache.modeMin: min (cache final layers only, smaller bucket)
buildCache.clearedMore: Deleted {{deleted}} objects. More remain, clear again.
buildCache.storedUnder: Layers are stored under {{prefix}}. Turn this off to opt this app out of the default.
buildCache.globalHint: Applies to every app without its own setting. Each app caches under build-cache/<app>/.
buildCache.notConfiguredTitle: Build cache is not configured on this server
buildCache.loadFailedTitle: Could not load build cache settings
buildCache.notConfiguredBody: Set APP_MASTER_KEY and restart the control plane to connect object storage.
buildCache.noDestinationBody: Connect a bucket under Settings, Storage destinations, then use it as a build cache here.
buildCache.usingDefault: Using the default build cache for all apps. Save a setting below to override it for this app.
buildCache.ranWithout: Last build ran without the cache
buildCache.title: Build cache
buildCache.description: Keep BuildKit layers in a storage destination so rebuilds skip unchanged steps. A cache problem never fails a build, it is reported as a warning.

description.gitlab: Register a GitLab OAuth application, then authorize it. gitlab.com and self-managed instances can be connected side by side.
description.bitbucket: Register a Bitbucket OAuth consumer, then authorize it. Add a second consumer later for another workspace.
description.gitea: Register a Gitea OAuth application, then authorize it. Each Gitea or Forgejo server is its own connection.
description.forgejo: Register a Forgejo OAuth application, then authorize it. Codeberg and self-hosted servers are each their own connection.
description.bitbucket_server: Create a personal access token on your Bitbucket Server, then add it here. Each server or account is its own connection.

gitConnections.scopeNote: Connections belong to this control plane and are managed by admins. Anyone allowed to read repositories can browse what an account can see.

disconnect.title: Disconnect {{label}}?
disconnect.description: This control plane stops using this account and revokes its token at the provider where that is supported. Other connected accounts are not touched.
disconnect.sources_one: {{count}} git source uses this account. It stays, shows needs reconnect, and works again once you connect an account on the same host.
disconnect.sources_other: {{count}} git sources use this account. They stay, show needs reconnect, and work again once you connect an account on the same host.

add.description: Create the OAuth application on the provider with redirect URI {{callback}}, then enter it here. You will be sent to the provider to authorize it.
add.applicationHelp: Reuse the same application to sign in with a different account on the same instance.
add.instanceHelp: gitlab.com or a self-managed address, for example https://git.example.com.
add.label: Label (optional)
add.labelHelp: Defaults to the account name once you authorize. You can rename it later.
add.tokenDescription: Create a personal access token on the server with repository read and write permission, then paste it here. It is verified, then stored encrypted.
add.tokenHelp: Under Manage account, Personal access tokens. The token is never shown again.
add.instanceHelpServer: The base address of your server, for example https://bitbucket.example.com.
add.testOk: Connected. The server answered and the details look right.

bad_url.message: That address does not look like this kind of server.
bad_url.fix: Use the root address of the instance, for example https://git.example.com, without a repository path.

bad_token.fix: Create a new personal access token with repository read access and paste it again.

tls.message: The server's TLS certificate was rejected.
tls.fix: Install a trusted certificate on the server, or add your private CA to this control plane's trust store.

unreachable.message: This control plane could not reach the server.
unreachable.fix: Check the hostname and port, and that the network or firewall allows outbound access to it.

toast.addedBody: Authorize it with the provider to finish.
toast.authorizedBody: Its repositories are now available to pick from.
